title: Rotations briefing — appendix & quick-failover templates
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact appendix for rotation briefs: quick checks, short triage flows, and tiny failover templates you can paste into Slack or an incident ticket. Not a replacement for the canonical runbook — think "cheat-sheet + local quirks" for the person taking the next shift.

How to use: paste the relevant snippet into the incident description or run as-is in the pager thread. Keep it short, update after any non-trivial play.

Shift start checklist (2 minutes):
- Pager feed: verify Unrouted Alerts group (Dash -> Alerts -> Unacked > filter: "unrouted") is empty.
- Key dashboards: open metrics: latency-api, token-cost-per-minute, kv-cache-hit, worker-queue-depth.
- Token budget: glance at billing dashboard (today usage vs budget). If >60% of daily budget used in first 6 hours, flag in handoff.
- Scheduled work: check /oncall/calendar for DB maintenance or model rollouts.

Quick triage flow (first 10 minutes):
1) Scope: single-request vs whole region? Check Grafana -> "request-err-rate" by region.
2) If single region: check region-specific infra (k8s nodes, AZ-network). If spike in pod restarts, go to k8s.
3) If global: suspect shared dependency (auth, kv-cache, model store). Check envoy errors and model-store latency.
4) Mitigation: if errors >5% and latency doubled, enable canary fallback: route traffic to last-known-good model tag (see Template A).

Template A — rollback to last-known-good model (hosted API fallback):
- When: model regressions or 5xx spike after rollout.
- Steps:
  1. Console -> Models -> Select model -> Rollout history -> identify tag "prod-stable-YYYYMMDD".
  2. API (if console slow): curl -X POST $REDWOOD_API/rollouts/rollback -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"<model-id>","tag":"prod-stable-YYYYMMDD"}'
  3. Verify: token-latency and 5xx drop within 2 minutes.
  4. Notify: post to #oncall-ops with subject "Rollback: <model> -> prod-stable-YYYYMMDD" and link to PR that introduced change.

Template B — emergency worker restart (k8s)
- When: worker pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff or KV cache thrash and mem growth >80%
- Steps (short):
  1. kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=serve-worker -o wide
  2. kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/serve-worker
  3. watch kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=serve-worker --no-headers -w
  4. If restarts don't stabilize in 3 minutes, scale down then up: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/serve-worker --replicas=0; sleep 10; kubectl -n inference scale deployment/serve-worker --replicas=6
  5. Post a short note in the pager thread with pod names replaced and immediate metrics (cpu/mem, queue length).

Template C — KV cache warm/clear (temporary):
- When: cache miss storms or corrupted prefix entries after model change
- Steps:
  1. Identify affected cache key prefixes in logs (prefix looks like "kv:cache:model:<model-id>:prefix").
  2. To clear only a prefix (preferred): ./tools/kv-admin --env prod --delete-prefix "kv:cache:model:<model-id>:prefix"
  3. If CLI unavailable fallback: restart cache daemon on affected hosts: systemctl restart redwood-kv-cache
  4. Monitor cache-hit metric; expect warm-up within 5-10 minutes.

Short diagnostics command list (copy-paste friendly):
- API health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq '.'
- Recent 5xx traces: curl -sS "https://observability/api/traces?service=redwood-api&status=5xx&since=10m" | head -n 30
- Model store latency: curl -sS https://metrics.internal/model-store/latency | tail -n 20
- Check worker queue depth: kubectl -n inference get hpa serve-worker -o yaml | yq '.status.currentMetrics'

Escalation matrix (fast):
- SRE oncall (primary): @oncall-sre -> first 15 minutes
- Serving runtime lead: @Priya Nair -> if issue persists past 20 minutes or post-rollback questions
- Product PM (hosted API): @Ethan Park -> if behavior is customer-facing and >30 minutes
- Eng manager on-call: escalate if business SLA risk or >2 hours unresolved

Notes to next person (template to paste in handoff):
- Current state: <one-line summary: e.g., "API latency normal, 5xx below 0.3% after worker restart at 01:12 UTC">
- Actions taken: <what I did and approximate times>
- Remaining items: <investigate logs in service X, check PR #1428 if recurrence>
- TODOs for next: <follow up with infra team on node OOMs, add circuit-breaker to route policy>

Known quirks / local memory (do not assume elsewhere):
- Model-store fallback is easier than restarting the whole serving cluster — use rollbacks first.
- When k8s API is slow, use the console's "restart group" (it talks to a different control plane).
- The warm cache script has a 30s backoff; don't run multiple warmers in parallel (they compete).
- During heavy token usage, the billing dashboard lags ~2–5 mins. Prefer recent metrics for triage, but use billing only for end-of-shift budget checks.

Open questions / TODO (action items for tribe):
- (TODO) Add a small endpoint that returns last rollout tag for model name — would speed rollback identification. Ref: GH PR #1428.
- (Question) Should warm-cache be rate-limited automatically when queue depth > 200? Ping @Priya.

Quick templates for Slack incident starter (paste into #oncall-ops):
- Short: "INCIDENT: <one-line> — scope: <region/global>. Action taken: <rollback/restart/clear-cache>. Owner: @<your-handle>. Timeline: <t0>. Details: <link to ticket/trace>"
- Longer (if paging): include the template A/B/C step you used and current metrics (latency/5xx/cache-hit).

Final reminders for the incoming oncall:
- If you inherit a rollback, look at the deploy PR diff (rare regressions are model-api changes, not runtime).
- When in doubt, communicate early — post a two-line update every 15 minutes to avoid duplicate work.
- Mark this doc with a timestamp and a one-line summary after significant plays so we can keep an informal timeline.

Personal style notes (Maya): keep the first message in a pager thread as a two-line TL;DR and one bullet with immediate next step. Saves time.

-- end appendix --

Revision history:
- 2024-10-02: initial sketches (Maya)
- 2024-11-14: added KV cache clear template after incident SRE-682 (Ethan)
- 2025-01-07: minor wording tweaks, added diagnostic commands (Maya)
